name: cut
summary: Remove sections from each line of input.
description: Selects columns, fields, or byte ranges from lines of files and standard input.

options.description: Use DELIM instead of tab as the field delimiter.

examples.title: Extract usernames
examples.explanation: Selects the first colon-delimited field.

examples.title: Select CSV columns
examples.explanation: Prints the first and third comma-separated fields.

examples.title: Select a byte range
examples.explanation: Extracts bytes two through four.

name: paste
summary: Merge lines of files side by side.
description: Writes corresponding lines from input files separated by tabs or a chosen delimiter.

options.description: Reuse characters from LIST as delimiters.
Paste one file at a time instead of in parallel.

examples.title: Join two columns
examples.explanation: Combines corresponding lines with tabs.

examples.title: Create CSV-like output
examples.explanation: Uses commas between corresponding values.

examples.title: Join a list into one line
examples.explanation: Serializes all lines from one file.

name: join
summary: Join lines of two files on a shared field.
description: Performs a relational-style join of two sorted files using a common field.

options.description: Use CHAR as the input and output field separator.

examples.title: Join two sorted tables
examples.explanation: Matches the default first field in both sorted files.

examples.title: Join CSV files
examples.explanation: Uses the first comma-delimited field as the key.

examples.title: Keep unmatched records
examples.explanation: Includes records found only in the first file.

name: sort
summary: Sort lines of text files.
description: Writes a sorted concatenation of all input files to standard output.

options.description: Sort using a key field definition.

examples.title: Sort names alphabetically
examples.explanation: Sorts lines using the locale comparison.

examples.title: Sort numeric values
examples.explanation: Compares values numerically rather than lexically.

examples.title: Sort by a column descending
examples.explanation: Uses the second field as a numeric reverse-order key.

name: uniq
summary: Report or omit repeated adjacent lines.
description: Filters adjacent matching lines; sort input first when duplicates may be separated.

examples.title: Remove adjacent duplicates
examples.explanation: Collapses only consecutive equal lines.

examples.title: Count event types
examples.explanation: Sorts first, then counts each repeated line.

examples.title: Show duplicates only
examples.explanation: Reports names appearing more than once.

name: wc
summary: Count lines, words, and bytes.
description: Prints newline, word, character, or byte counts for each input file.

examples.title: Count source lines
examples.explanation: Reports the number of newline characters.

examples.title: Count words in documentation
examples.explanation: Counts whitespace-delimited words.

examples.title: Count bytes in a file
examples.explanation: Reports the exact byte length.

name: tr
summary: Translate or delete characters.
description: Copies standard input to standard output while translating, squeezing, or deleting characters.

options.description: Squeeze repeated characters in the result.

examples.title: Convert lowercase to uppercase
examples.explanation: Maps each lowercase letter to its uppercase counterpart.

examples.title: Remove carriage returns
examples.explanation: Strips CR characters from a text stream.

examples.title: Collapse repeated spaces
examples.explanation: Squeezes runs of spaces into one.

name: tee
summary: Copy standard input to files and standard output.
description: Reads standard input and writes it both to standard output and to one or more files.

options.description: Append to files instead of overwriting them.

examples.title: Save and view command output
examples.explanation: Displays build output while saving a copy.

examples.title: Append to a log
examples.explanation: Adds the timestamp to an existing log.

examples.title: Write to two files
examples.explanation: Writes the same stream to both files and the terminal.

useCases: Writing one stream to multiple destinations

name: xargs
summary: Build and execute commands from standard input.
description: Constructs command lines from items read from standard input, with controls for batching and placement.

options.description: Use at most MAX-ARGS input items per command line.

examples.title: Run a command for each item
examples.explanation: Builds one printf invocation per input item.

examples.title: Handle filenames safely
examples.explanation: Uses NUL delimiters so spaces do not split names.

examples.title: Pass many arguments in batches
examples.explanation: Limits each invocation to two input arguments.

name: diff
summary: Compare files line by line.
description: Compares two files and reports changes needed to transform the first into the second.

examples.title: Compare configuration versions
examples.explanation: Shows a compact patch-style difference.

examples.title: Compare directories
examples.explanation: Reports changed and newly added files recursively.

examples.title: Check identical files
examples.explanation: Prints only whether files differ.

name: cmp
summary: Compare two files byte by byte.
description: Reports the first byte and line where two files differ, or confirms that they match.

options.description: Print byte numbers and differing byte values.
Produce no output and report status only.

examples.title: Find the first difference
examples.explanation: Reports the first mismatch.

examples.title: Check equality in a script
examples.explanation: Uses the exit status to indicate identical files.

examples.title: List all differing bytes
examples.explanation: Lists byte positions and values for differences.

name: comm
summary: Compare two sorted files line by line.
description: Produces three columns for lines unique to the first file, unique to the second, and common to both.

examples.title: Show all comparison columns
examples.explanation: Displays unique-first, unique-second, and common lines as columns.

examples.title: Find additions
examples.explanation: Suppresses columns to show lines only in the new file.

examples.title: Find lines removed
examples.explanation: Shows entries present only in the old file.

name: fmt
summary: Reformat paragraph text.
description: Fills and joins lines to create readable paragraphs while preserving indentation conventions.

options.description: Split long lines but do not join short lines.

examples.title: Wrap documentation
examples.output:
LinuxDocs is a reference for commands and authorized security
training tools.
examples.explanation: Reflows paragraphs to a target width.

examples.title: Format standard input
examples.explanation: Wraps the input at the selected width.

examples.title: Split only long lines
examples.output:
A short line remains
wrapped at twenty
columns.
examples.explanation: Avoids joining existing short lines.

name: fold
summary: Wrap each input line to a fixed width.
description: Writes input lines with a maximum width, breaking long lines without paragraph reflow.

options.description: Use WIDTH as the maximum line width.

examples.explanation: Breaks the line every ten columns.

examples.explanation: Breaks at a space instead of splitting a word.

examples.title: Wrap a file
examples.output:
LinuxDocs is a reference for Linux commands and authorized
security training tools.
examples.explanation: Limits displayed line width.

name: column
summary: Format input into aligned columns.
description: Formats delimited text into columns suitable for terminal display.

options.description: Create a table by determining column widths.
Use SEP as the input delimiter.

examples.title: Align whitespace data

id  name   role
1   alice  admin
2   bob    viewer

name: expand
summary: Convert tabs to spaces.

summary: Reverse characters on each line.
